strategy.summary: Densifying a datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray with a fill value that numpy cannot promote (nanosecond Timestamp/Timedelta, or fill in a different unit than the subtype, or np.nan with mixed boxing) yields an object array mixing datetime.datetime/ints with pandas scalars, and to_dense with an explicit dtype truncates ns fill values to microseconds. The fix routes both paths through _promote_for_fill. Reproduce by building pandas at the buggy commit 14de06cf2823 and running the two new sparse array tests, which should fail there and pass on the fixed revision.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) capable of building pandas Cython extensions
pinned_because: No documented version constraint for NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata or Cython was stated in the evidence; versions are unpinned and chosen by the strategy, not by documentation. Cython is documented as required for source builds (installable from PyPI), so it is installed explicitly before the editable build. tzdata is only required on Windows/Emscripten and is left to the default install here.

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_array.py::test_to_dense_datetimelike_non_numpy_fill and pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_array.py::test_to_dense_datetimelike_fill_other_unit and pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_indexing.py::TestSparseArrayIndexing::test_take_fill_datetimelike_string (parametrized over kind M8/m8, unit s/ms/us/ns, na_fill or boxed True/False)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 14de06cf2823 the new tests fail: to_dense/np.asarray(dtype=object) produce an object array with mixed datetime.datetime or integer entries beside the pandas fill value, and ns fill values are truncated to us under to_dense(dtype=...) so the equality assertions against the dense values fail. On the fixed revision (the PR merge that routes through _promote_for_fill) all parametrizations of these tests pass, with dense results of datetime64/timedelta64 dtype in the subtype unit and the fill converted to that unit.
strategy.numerical_probe: Construct SparseArray(np.array([1,2,3],dtype='M8[s]'), fill_value=pd.Timestamp(np.datetime64(2,'s')).as_unit('ns')) with a gap, then compare arr.to_dense() and np.asarray(arr, dtype='i8') against the dense values.
risks: The defect is a dtype/boxing behaviour, not a platform-specific floating-point effect, so it should reproduce on any platform with a working pandas build; however the exact numpy version matters because np.full and datetime boxing of mismatched units changed across numpy releases, and no numpy constraint is documented, so the buggy behaviour may only appear on some numpy versions.

Fill value unit must differ from the subtype unit to trigger the truncation/integer read; the na_fill=True branch uses np.nan, which may not exercise the ns truncation at all, so the failing signal for that parametrization may come from the object-dtype mixing only.
Requires explicit numeric dtype in to_dense or Series.to_numpy for the integer-cast branch; the object-dtype branch needs dtype=None (astype(object)).
Sparse array must contain gaps (ngaps >= 1); the tests assert this, so an unexpected sp_index layout would fail for reasons unrelated to the bug.
Test selection is by -k across two files; if the test_indexing.py test is not collected under that class name, selection silently drops it, so verify collection counts before trusting a pass.
Building from source needs a compiler and Cython; if the build fails, the transition cannot be observed at all, so the environment must be validated first.

If the buggy revision was observed on a platform with different integer width or locale behaviour, the test may pass on buggy code on this host; no platform was stated in the evidence so none is assumed.

oracle.reference_source: dense result of the same values array (tm.assert_numpy_array_equal against the original datetime64/timedelta64 values)
oracle.why: The fix's correctness is established by equality of the sparse-densified result with the dense numpy array, with no numerical tolerance involved.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 14de06cf2823 the object-dtype comparison receives an array whose stored entries are datetime.datetime or ints beside the pandas fill, and the to_dense(dtype) path truncates an ns fill to us, so tm.assert_numpy_array_equal against the dense values raises an AssertionError on dtype or element mismatch.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision _promote_for_fill normalizes the fill to a numpy scalar in the subtype unit, so dense and object conversions match the dense values exactly and all parametrizations pass.
